## Summary

I implemented the city title-casing behavior in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`:

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — added city resolution during owner creation:
- Added `owner.setCity(resolveCity(owner.getCity()))` before the customer code is assigned, so the resolved spelling flows into both the stored `city` field and the returned DTO.
- `resolveCity(String city)` — looks for any existing owner whose city matches case-insensitively; if found, reuses that owner's **exact** stored spelling. Otherwise it title-cases the supplied value. Null-safe.
- `titleCase(String value)` — upper-cases the first letter of each whitespace-separated word and lower-cases the rest, preserving original whitespace (e.g. `"LONDON"` → `"London"`, `"new york"` → `"New York"`).

**`OwnerRestControllerV1Tests.java`** — added two tests:
- `createOwnerTitleCasesCityWhenNoOwnerExistsInThatCity` — posts `"new  YORK"` (no existing owner) and asserts the returned city is `"New  York"`.
- `createOwnerReusesExistingCitySpelling` — posts `"mcfarland"`, where seed data already has an owner in `"McFarland"`, and asserts the returned city reuses the exact spelling `"McFarland"` (which plain title-casing would incorrectly produce as `"Mcfarland"`).

The change composes cleanly with the existing customer-code logic (which already uppercases the city) — the `CARDIFF-0002` sequential-code test still passes.
